texts: The Waterston shunt is an anastomosis between the right PA and the ascending aorta: D.
It was made side to side, behind the ascending aorta, to send more blood to the lungs in cyanotic babies.

Like the Potts shunt (descending aorta to left PA), its size was hard to judge, so it often flooded the lungs, caused pulmonary hypertension or kinked the right PA; the modified Blalock-Taussig shunt replaced both.
The Glenn joins the SVC to the right PA, and the classic Blalock-Taussig shunt the subclavian artery to the pulmonary artery.
In the picture, the stonemason Waterston cuts a round stone window from the orca's front climb into the right money pipe behind it.
Memory hook: WATER-STONE: a stone window from the rising orca to the right money pipe.
